1201	## 8. The deprecated row engine
1202	
1203	**This section is stale — the package it describes no longer exists.** It originally said
1204	`pkg/query/logical/measure` would reject all three new shapes (`agg.tag_name`, `COUNT_DISTINCT`,
1205	`group_by.time_bucket`) with a `--measure-vectorized-enabled=true` message, on the reasoning that
1206	implementing parity in the row iterators would roughly double the work to protect a rollback path
1207	that was itself being retired.
1208	
1209	That rollback path was removed outright — `chore: remove the row-based query path from measure,
1210	stream and trace` (#1326) deleted `pkg/query/logical/measure` entirely, *before* this design doc
1211	was even merged (#1326 landed 2026-09-16; #1360 merged 2026-09-17). There is no row-path analyzer
1212	left to add a guard to, for any of the three shapes, because there is no row path. The
1213	`--measure-vectorized-enabled` flag itself is now a no-op compatibility shim
1214	(`removedRowQueryFlag` in `banyand/measure/measure.go`): `=true` (or omitting the flag) is
1215	accepted; `=false` hard-fails at startup with `"row-based query was removed in 0.12.0, see
1216	apache/skywalking#13998"`. The vectorized engine (`pkg/query/vectorized/measure`) is the only
1217	engine, and each new shape's validation lives directly in its analyzer
1218	(`pkg/query/vectorized/measure/plan/analyzer.go`) rather than in a parallel rejection guard.
1219	
1220	---
1221	
1222	## 9. Alternatives considered
1223	
1224	| Alternative | Why rejected |
1225	|---|---|
1226	| **Aggregate inside the native inverted index** | The engine already aggregates locally on data nodes, so this would not reduce network cost — it only moves which layer owns local aggregation, while duplicating grouping, arithmetic, memory accounting and distributed reduction. Estimated 5–8+ engineer-weeks against 2–4 for extending the engine. |
1227	| **HyperLogLog partials** | Constant wire cost and no decomposability condition to check, but it needs a new partial wire type and an API contract about error bounds. §7.4 already gets cardinality-independent wire *exactly* whenever the condition holds, which covers the motivating shape — so a sketch would buy only the queries §7.4 rejects, and would buy them approximately. That is the right thing to revisit if those rejections turn out to matter, and the wrong thing to build speculatively. |
1228	| **A value-shipping fallback** for queries that fail the condition — nodes ship distinct values, liaison unions | Always correct and needs no condition check, but its wire volume and liaison memory scale with cardinality, so a single query can funnel every value into shared infrastructure. It also doubles the surface: two implementations, a static chooser, opposite replica-dedup requirements, and a differential test to keep them honest. Rejecting is consistent with how this design treats every other unsupported shape. §7.4. |
1229	| **Ship per-node counts and sum them** | Wrong. A value appearing on two nodes is counted twice; that is the same class of bug as the multi-bucket `COUNT(*)` this design removes. |
1230	| **Emit an explicit set-typed partial column** | Same wire volume as shipping distinct tuples, but needs a new column type, a new frame wire type, and a new `Partial` shape. Reusing the group-by shape costs nothing extra. |
1231	| **Solve it upstream instead** — change SkyWalking to store labelled metric values as tags | An OAP core change touching all three storage plugins, and it multiplies row count by label cardinality — the packed representation exists precisely to prevent that. Out of scope here regardless, since it does not remove the need for `COUNT_DISTINCT`. |
1232	| **Requiring the width to be a multiple of `Measure.interval`** | Rejected after the fact that motivated it turned out not to hold: `interval` is a declared write cadence, not a storage invariant, so data points do not reliably land on interval boundaries. With arbitrary timestamps every width bins just as meaningfully as any other, and the rule would refuse useful queries to protect an alignment that was never guaranteed. §5.3. |
1233	| **A `multiplier` integer instead of a duration string** | Makes invalid widths unrepresentable, but `multiplier: 5` cannot be read without the measure schema in hand — it means 5 minutes or 5 hours depending on the measure. A duration string matches `Measure.interval`'s own encoding, parses with the same helper, and matches the `INTERVAL <width>` spelling the bucketing functions in §1 use. Validation is one modulo. |
1234	| **Bucket on `segment_interval`** rather than `Measure.interval` | `ResourceOpts.segment_interval` is an `IntervalRule` restricted to HOUR/DAY and describes physical segmentation, not data-point cadence. It is both too coarse and semantically unrelated. |
1235	| **Hash-map the bucket** — add it to `keyIndices` and hold every `(bucket, tags…)` until the scan ends | The path of least resistance, and wrong for a time-series database. It holds `buckets × tagGroups` live groups (1440× for a day at 1-minute), blocks all output until the last row, and then needs a sort to restore time order — all three paid for information the scan already provides, since measure results arrive timestamp-ascending by default (`query.go:286`). §7.2 streams instead. |
1236	| **Reuse the TopN RPC for series** | `TopNResponse.lists` is already a per-timestamp series, but the RPC ranks a single pre-aggregated field by a pre-declared `TopNAggregation` rule. It cannot express an ad-hoc `COUNT_DISTINCT` over a tag, and it requires schema registration ahead of the query. |
1237	
1238	---
1239	
1240	## 10. Compatibility and follow-ups
1241	
1242	- **Wire.** All three API additions are additive. Old clients never set `tag_name` or
1243	  `time_bucket`, and never receive a `COUNT_DISTINCT` response.
1244	- **No new configuration.** `COUNT_DISTINCT` either pushes down or the request is rejected, so
1245	  there is no flag, no default to choose and no second path to keep warm. The §7.4 per-shard
1246	  partial ships as part of that single path rather than behind a gate, and is correct on its own
1247	  terms; only the question of whether it *also* fixes a live defect in `SUM`/`COUNT` is deferred
1248	  to the parallel experiment.
1249	- **Mixed-version clusters.** A liaison that sends a `COUNT_DISTINCT` request to an older data
1250	  node gets the node's existing unknown-function error rather than a wrong number, because
1251	  `protoAggFuncToInternal` (`plan.go:167`) rejects enum values it does not know. **`time_bucket`
1252	  has no such guard** — an old node silently ignores the unknown proto field and returns
1253	  whole-range partials, which the liaison would otherwise reduce into one row per tag group with
1254	  no error: a series collapsed to a point, silently.
1255	
1256	  The check is **self-describing**, needing no capability negotiation. A bucketed query's partial
1257	  carries a `RoleTimestamp` column, because §7.2 reverses D2 exactly when a bucket key is
1258	  present. A node that ignored the field emits partials *without* that column, so the liaison
1259	  detects the absence directly and hard-errors. This is deliberately not a node-version or
1260	  capability lookup: `database.v1.Node` carries only `metadata`, `roles`, addresses and a generic
1261	  `labels` map, so no such mechanism exists to consult — and inventing one to answer a question
1262	  the data already answers would be the wrong trade.
1263	- **`limit` with a bucketed query.** Result rows are `buckets × tagGroups`, so the default
1264	  `limit` of 100 (`measure_analyzer.go:32 defaultLimit`) truncates a 1-hour/1-minute/50-device
1265	  series at 100 of its 3000 rows. The default is left alone — changing it would alter unbucketed
1266	  queries too — but clients must set `limit` explicitly, and this needs to be prominent in the
1267	  BydbQL docs rather than buried in the API reference.
1268	- **Possible follow-up: multiple aggregates, then aliases.** Out of scope here by decision (§3),
1269	  and recorded only so the route stays visible if the remainder of §1.1 is ever wanted.
1270	  `AggSpec` is already a slice and `BatchAggregation` already loops over `a.aggs`, so the
1271	  constraint is the singular `QueryRequest.agg` field and BydbQL's one-aggregate rule — API and
1272	  planning, not execution. Aliases need a BydbQL `AS` production and an
1273	  `Aggregation.output_name` field together, and the two share one question: what a result column
1274	  is called when there is more than one.
1275	- **Follow-up: per-bucket `top`.** If demand appears, the honest move is to extend the TopN RPC
1276	  rather than overload `QueryRequest.top`, since TopN already returns a per-timestamp series.
1277	- **Follow-up: gap filling.** Needs a declared bucket set and a zero value per aggregate; SUM and
1278	  COUNT fill with 0, MIN/MAX/MEAN have no defensible fill.
1279	
1280	### Fixed: adjacent inconsistency in the liaison-side key resolution
1281	
1282	`reduce.go resolveKeyIndices` used to match key tags by `Name` only, ignoring `TagFamily`, unlike
1283	`plan.go:140` and `distributed.go:945`, which both compare the family. An earlier version of
1284	this note claimed that was safe because "tag names are unique per measure" — that directly
1285	contradicts §5.1 above, which debunks exactly that assumption (tag-family validation does not
1286	reject a name repeated across families, and `pkg/query/vectorized/schema_test.go` exercises it
1287	as a valid case). A bucketed or tag-keyed distributed reduce over such a schema could silently
1288	bind to the wrong family's column. Fixed by threading the key's `TagFamily` alongside its names
1289	end to end — `distributedGroupByTagKey` (`distributed.go`) now returns `(family, names)` instead
1290	of discarding the family, and `resolveKeyIndices` matches on `(family, name)`, same as `plan.go`
1291	and `distributed.go`'s row-merge path.
1292	
1293	---
1294	
1295	## 11. Testing strategy
1296	
1297	**Unit**
1298	
1299	- `pkg/query/aggregation` — **this package has no tests at all today.** Add set semantics, reset,
1300	  and the `NewMap`/`NewReduce` rejection that guards the TopN path.
1301	- `vectorized/measure/aggregation_test.go` — its `aggIntSchema()`/`aggFloatSchema()` fixtures use
1302	  a `RoleField` agg column exclusively; they need a tag-input sibling. Cover the numeric
1303	  functions over an INT tag, `COUNT` over a string tag, `COUNT_DISTINCT` over string/int/bytes,
1304	  null exclusion, budget exhaustion on a high-cardinality set, and the distinct-tuple map shape.
1305	- `vectorized/measure/plan_test.go:73-78` enumerates the five functions explicitly and must gain
1306	  the sixth; likewise `test/cases/measure/cmd/generate/layer3_features.go:197`, which hard-codes
1307	  `{"MEAN","MAX","MIN","COUNT","SUM"}` in the generated feature matrix. Both under-cover a new
1308	  function silently — the `exhaustive` linter will not catch either, because the enum switches
1309	  have `default` branches.
1310	- `plan/analyzer_test.go` — the full §6 rejection matrix, plus implicit projection and `HideTag`.
1311	  For bucketing, the §5.3 table is the test table: width from the request; width absent but
1312	  interval present; both absent (reject); unparseable, zero and negative widths (reject). A width
1313	  that is *not* a multiple of the interval must be **accepted** — that is the case the removed
1314	  rule would have wrongly rejected.
1315	- `plan/distributed_test.go` — node template, liaison reduce over synthetic frames, replica
1316	  idempotence, and `top` + `offset` over the distinct result.
1317	- **The `COUNT_DISTINCT` push-down condition (§7.4) is the thing to test hardest**, because a
1318	  mis-evaluated condition does not crash — it returns an inflated count that looks entirely
1319	  plausible. There is no fallback path to diff against, so the tests must pin the predicate
1320	  directly and pin the rejection.
1321	  - **Accept/reject table over schemas**, driven by `routingTags` not entity tags:
1322	    `routingTags ⊆ groupBy ∪ target` (accept); a routing tag in neither (reject); `index_mode`
1323	    with the same containment (**accept** — §7.4); an unresolvable tag, routing key or stage
1324	    (reject — indeterminate must not be permissive, and must not panic).
1325	  - **The sharding-key counterexample**, which an entity-based rule accepts and must not: entity
1326	    `{e}`, sharding key `{s}`, rows carrying the same `e` under two `s` values, and
1327	    `COUNT_DISTINCT(e)` with no grouping on `s`. Must reject. Summing scalar partials here
1328	    returns 2 for one distinct entity.
1329	  - **Multi-stage rejection**: the same query must be rejected when the resolved stage set has
1330	    more than one entry, bucketed or not — and the resolution must expand `DefaultStages`, not
1331	    only an explicit `stages` list. Pair it with the positive case: the same target in two
1332	    *disjoint buckets* of a single stage must count once per bucket and must **not** be rejected
1333	    for that reason.
1334	  - **Ambiguous tag name**: two families each containing `region`; an aggregation naming `region`
1335	    must resolve by its family qualifier, and an unqualified reference must fail naming both
1336	    families rather than silently binding to whichever family `RegisterTag` wrote last.
1337	  - **The rejection is a contract, not an implementation detail.** Assert the error is returned
1338	    at analyze time, before any node is contacted, and that its text names the target, the
1339	    entity, and the two ways out. A test on the message is warranted here because the message is
1340	    the entire remediation path for a user who has hit it.
1341	  - **An overlapping fixture must be rejected, not silently summed**: the same distinct value
1342	    present on two shards for one group. This is precisely the data shape that makes push-down
1343	    wrong, so what is under test is that the condition catches it rather than that the arithmetic
1344	    handles it.
1345	  - **Replica duplication must be deduped**: feed the same `(stage, shard, group)` partial twice
1346	    and assert the count does not double. Then feed two partials differing only in shard, and
1347	    assert they *do* add — the two halves of §7.4(c), which fail in opposite directions.
1348	  - **Standalone/distributed agreement**: the same query and fixture must return the same number
1349	    single-node and across nodes. Single-node has no sharding, so this is the cheapest end-to-end
1350	    check that the partition arithmetic is right.
1351	  - **Replicated-topology agreement** (§7.4): the same query and fixture must return the same
1352	    number at `replicas=0` and `replicas=1`. This is the regression test the per-shard partial
1353	    exists for, and it is the one that would have caught the defect the 4a experiment is
1354	    investigating — so it belongs in the suite permanently, not just in the investigation.
1355	- **Bucketing needs its own unit coverage**, and two properties matter more than the happy path:
1356	  - `bucketStart` agrees with `getWindowStart` (`sliding_window.go:302`) across a table of
1357	    timestamps and widths, including a boundary timestamp (`ts % width == 0` stays put) and a
1358	    negative one. Asserting the two formulas agree keeps the query path and the TopN
1359	    pre-aggregation path from drifting into two definitions of "the 5-minute bucket".
1360	  - `plan/build_test.go:221` currently asserts the output schema drops the timestamp. That
1361	    assertion must stay for the unbucketed case and gain a bucketed sibling asserting the
1362	    timestamp **is** present and carries the bucket start — the two together pin D2 as
1363	    conditional rather than repealed.
1364	  - **`COUNT` and `COUNT_DISTINCT` must be allowed to disagree at the interval width.** An
1365	    earlier draft proposed asserting they are *equal* when bucketed at exactly
1366	    `Measure.interval`, on the belief that storage holds one row per `(entity, bucket)`. It does
1367	    not — the interval is a declared write cadence (§5.3) — so that test would fail on perfectly
1368	    legal data. Invert it: seed one entity with two off-cadence points inside one bucket
1369	    (`09:01:00` and `09:01:34` on a 1-minute measure) and assert `COUNT` reports 2 while
1370	    `COUNT_DISTINCT` reports 1. That is the whole reason the function exists, and it is the
1371	    fixture a naive implementation passes only by accident.
1372	- **The §7.7 metadata shortcut needs its range guard tested**: one block with rows at 09:00 and
1373	  09:59 (a single hourly bucket) queried over 09:30–09:31 must yield **no** bucket row; the same
1374	  block fully inside the range must take the shortcut. Without the first case the optimisation
1375	  reports buckets that contain nothing.
1376	- **Index-mode ordering** (§7.2): index-mode rows whose index order is deliberately
1377	  non-chronological — timestamps arriving A, B, A — must still produce one result per bucket. This
1378	  is the case that proves index mode took the map rather than the streaming operator, and it fails
1379	  loudly if someone later "optimises" it onto the streaming path.
1380	- **The streaming operator needs tests for the property it depends on, not just its output**
1381	  (§7.2):
1382	  - **Bucket closure**: after the input advances past bucket *n*, the operator has released
1383	    bucket *n*'s groups. Assert on live state, not just emitted rows — a version that emits
1384	    correctly while retaining everything passes an output-only test and fails the whole point of
1385	    the design.
1386	  - **Monotonicity guard**: feed deliberately out-of-order timestamps and assert a loud error
1387	    rather than duplicate rows for a reopened bucket. This is the silent-corruption path, so it
1388	    needs a test that would fail if someone later removes the check as redundant.
1389	  - **Pipelining**: the first bucket's output is available before the source is exhausted. A
1390	    `BreakerOperator`-shaped implementation passes every correctness test and fails this one.
1391	  - **Ordering assumption**: a test pinning `applyMeasureQueryOrdering`'s `Order == nil` →
1392	    `orderByTS = true` default (`query.go:286`), since the streaming operator's correctness rests
1393	    on it and nothing in the vec package would otherwise notice if that default changed.
1394	
1395	**Integration** — `test/cases/measure/`
1396	
1397	Cases are `input/<name>.yaml` + `input/<name>.ql` + golden `want/<name>.yaml`, registered as a
1398	`g.Entry` in `measure.go`; `data.go verifyQLWithRequest` proto-compares the QL transform against
1399	the YAML request, so both inputs are required.
1400	
1401	The load-bearing case is a **multi-bucket cardinality fixture**: one user with 3 api-keys spread
1402	across 3 hour buckets, a second user with 2, asserting `3` and `2` for the scalar case and the
1403	correct ordering for the ranked, paged case. It must run in the **distributed** suite
1404	(`test/integration/distributed/query/vectorized_test.go`, liaison + 2 data nodes) as well as
1405	standalone — the cross-node union has no single-node analogue, and a fixture confined to one
1406	bucket is exactly what lets the naive `COUNT(*)` over-count slip through unnoticed.
1407

## Summary

Note: the Bash tool was unavailable in this job (`Read-only jobs cannot execute shell commands`), so git history was reconstructed by reading plain-text git internals directly (`packed-refs`, `logs/refs/heads/*`) rather than running `git log`.

### 1. CHANGES.md entries (root: `/mnt/d/skywalking-banyandb/graphloom/879ee04f-e57/CHANGES.md`, `## 0.12.0`)

- **Tag aggregation (shipped, partial):**
  > "`measure.v1.QueryRequest.Aggregation` can now target a tag (`tag_name` + `tag_family`) instead of a field: `SUM`/`MIN`/`MAX`/`MEAN` over an `INT` tag, and `COUNT` over any scalar tag, in both standalone and distributed queries. Wire-additive only... **`COUNT_DISTINCT` is not yet implemented**; see the [tag aggregation and time bucketing design](docs/design/0.12.0/tag-aggregation/README.md)."

- **Time bucketing (shipped):**
  > "`measure.v1.QueryRequest.GroupBy.time_bucket` groups a measure query by tumbling time windows, alone or combined with a tag `GroupBy`, in both standalone and distributed queries... index-mode measures... use a bounded non-streaming fallback instead."

- **Design doc itself (this is PR #1360):**
  > "Add the [tag aggregation and time bucketing design](docs/design/0.12.0/tag-aggregation/README.md) for the measure query engine, covering aggregation over tags, `COUNT_DISTINCT`, and `GROUP BY` time buckets."

No CHANGES.md entry contains "COUNT_DISTINCT" as shipped, nor the literal strings "local scan", "run-fold", "metadata-only", or "index-resolved" — those appear only in the design doc (§7.7/§12), not in CHANGES.md. The literal string "#1360" does not appear in CHANGES.md; this repo's changelog style omits PR numbers (PR #1360 corresponds to the design-doc-addition commit itself).

### 2/3. What landed, via `packed-refs` + branch reflogs (git log unavailable)

- `feat/tag-agg-14088` → `916ddd8c2` "feat(query): allow measure Agg to target a tag, not just a field" — **stage 1**, shipped.
- `feat/time-bucket-14089` → `88fe70aca`/`e48e23db7` "feat(query): group measure queries by time bucket" + distributed/drain fix — **stages 2–3**, shipped.
- `feat/measure-tag-aggregation` → `5b0e85401` "docs(design): add tag aggregation and time bucketing design for 0.12.0" (this is PR #1360).
- `feat/count-distinct-14090` → 20+ commits ending `2cc31847a` implementing single-node and distributed `COUNT_DISTINCT`, memory charging, BydbQL/bydbctl, tests — covers **stages 4–8**. These commits exist locally but are **not reflected in main's CHANGES.md** (which still says "not yet implemented"), and the current HEAD (`cb15c9110`, same as `main`) matches the worktree base — so this branch appears unmerged/not yet shipped.
- **No commit, reflog entry, or branch anywhere mentions "run-fold", "run-folding", "metadata-only", "local scan", or "index-resolved"** — stages 8a and 9 have zero implementation history.

### 3. Open branch/PR search

`packed-refs` (full file, 383 lines, all local/remote branches and tags) contains no branch matching `run-fold`, `local-scan`, or `metadata`. Nothing in-flight for stage 8a/9.

### 4. Confirmation

Shipped per CHANGES.md: stage 1 (tag-targeted SUM/MIN/MAX/MEAN/COUNT) and stages 2–3 (time bucketing). **Not shipped**: COUNT_DISTINCT (explicitly flagged "not yet implemented" even though a feature branch exists), and **stage 8a (run-folding) and stage 9 (metadata-only scan) are confirmed absent** — no CHANGES.md entry, no commit, no branch — exactly as expected for optional, undelivered stages.
